body_markdown:
A license to use copyrighted music can sometimes be transferred, but permission does not automatically follow a video, campaign or business to its new owner. The answer depends on the rights granted, the agreement’s assignment provisions, the transaction structure and applicable law.


For labels, publishers, agencies and acquiring companies, the practical question is whether the intended user will actually have permission after the handoff. A purchase agreement between buyer and seller cannot, by itself, expand the music rights the seller received.


## What counts as transferring a music license?


Several different transactions get described as a “transfer,” even though they have different legal effects.


Arrangement


What changes


Main clearance question


Assignment


Another party takes over licensed rights


Does the license permit assignment, and is consent required?


Sublicense


The original licensee grants another party permission under its license


Does the original grant authorize sublicensing?


Contractor access


An editor, agency or production vendor uses the music for the licensee


Does the agreement cover that contractor’s activities?


Copyright ownership transfer


Ownership of specified copyright rights changes hands


What rights are being conveyed, and are the transfer formalities satisfied?


Change of control


Ownership of the licensee changes


Does the contract treat that transaction as requiring approval?


Delivering an editable project file is not necessarily an assignment. An editor may be authorized to work for a licensed brand without receiving any independent permission to reuse the track.


Likewise, transferring a license to use copyrighted music does not necessarily transfer the underlying copyright or release the original licensee from its obligations.


## When can you transfer a license to use copyrighted music?


Start with the agreement, but do not stop there. U.S. copyright law and the law governing the contract can affect whether a transfer is effective.


### Nonexclusive permission usually needs particular care


Under U.S. law, nonexclusive copyright licenses are generally treated as personal to the licensee and nonassignable without the licensor’s consent. An agreement may provide that consent in advance, such as by expressly allowing assignment to a qualifying business purchaser.


If the contract says nothing about assignment, do not assume silence gives permission. Have counsel assess the applicable rule before relying on the license after a sale or handoff.


### Exclusive grants require a different analysis


An exclusive license can convey ownership of particular copyright rights.[Section 101 of the Copyright Act](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/17/101) includes exclusive licenses within the definition of a transfer of copyright ownership, while excluding nonexclusive licenses.


That distinction does not mean every exclusive license is freely assignable. Contract restrictions, the particular rights conveyed and governing law still matter.[Section 201(d)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/17/201) recognizes that copyright ownership can be divided and transferred in separate parts.


The safe conclusion is narrower than “exclusive means transferable”: a license to use copyrighted music must be evaluated against both its contractual restrictions and its legal character.


## Check both the composition and the recording


Music clearance often involves two separate copyrights: the composition, usually controlled by songwriters or publishers, and the sound recording, often controlled by a label or artist.


For a video using an existing recording, the relevant permissions commonly include a synchronization license for the composition and a master-use license for the recording. Their assignment terms may differ.


For example, a publisher might permit assignment to the purchaser of a licensed film, subject to notice. The master owner might require prior written consent for that same transaction. Approval from one does not resolve the other.


If the ownership or administration chain is unclear, begin by[identifying who controls the song and recording](https://usethirdchair.com/blog/copyright-search-how-to-find-who-owns-a-song-or-video) . Confirm who has authority to approve the transfer, including whether an administrator can consent on behalf of the relevant owners.


For each license to use copyrighted music, record the approving party, covered rights, licensed entity and applicable restrictions. Where several agreements cover the same production, treat clearance as incomplete until every necessary permission supports the proposed handoff.


## How business transactions affect existing permissions


The transaction structure matters because a new shareholder is not necessarily a new licensee, while an asset purchaser usually is.


### Asset sales


Buying a film library, advertising campaign or brand’s assets does not automatically carry every associated music agreement with it. The parties need to identify which licenses are included and whether each can be assigned.


A seller’s promise that “all necessary rights transfer” allocates risk between buyer and seller. It does not bind a music rights holder that has not authorized the transfer.


### Stock purchases and mergers


In a stock purchase, the licensed company may remain the same legal entity. Even then, a change-of-control clause can trigger notice, consent or another contractual consequence.


Mergers require separate analysis. Their effect can depend on the transaction structure, governing law and contract language, including provisions addressing transfers “by operation of law.”


### Agency-to-client handoffs


An agency may have obtained permission expressly for a named client, or it may hold a license limited to its own activities. Those arrangements are not interchangeable.


Before closing any transaction, map each license to use copyrighted music to the actual entity that will exploit the content afterward. Do not rely solely on the name appearing on the invoice.


## A permitted transfer does not expand the permitted use


Even an authorized assignment generally carries the existing license limits forward. It does not automatically add new platforms, territories, media or campaign purposes.


Suppose a brand licensed a track for six months of organic Instagram posts. A permitted assignment to an acquiring company would not, by itself, authorize paid YouTube advertising, television use or another six months of publication.


Review the grant against the proposed activity, including:


-


**Media and platforms:** Organic social posts, paid advertising, websites, podcasts, television or other specified channels.


-


**Term and territory:** The remaining license period and authorized geographic coverage.


-


**Content and edits:** The approved production, cutdowns, alternate versions and any permitted adaptations.


-


**Users and accounts:** The named licensee, approved affiliates, client entities and publishing accounts.


-


**Commercial context:** The covered brand, product, campaign and any prohibited associations.


Platform-provided permissions need separate attention. A track available through a platform’s music tools is not automatically cleared for export, another account or off-platform distribution.


When reviewing a license to use copyrighted music, treat transferability and permitted use as two independent checks. Passing one does not satisfy the other.


## How to document a transfer properly


A useful transfer process produces a clear record of who may use the music, for what purpose and from what date. It should also resolve obligations that survive the handoff.


### Assemble the complete agreement


Collect the executed license, schedules, incorporated terms, amendments and relevant approvals. An invoice or download receipt may not contain the full grant or restrictions.


Locate the assignment, sublicensing, affiliate-use and change-of-control provisions. Check notice requirements, approval procedures, transfer fees and any exceptions for business sales or internal reorganizations.


Language such as “binding on successors and assigns” deserves attention, but it should not be treated as a substitute for reviewing the actual assignment provisions. Its effect depends on the agreement as a whole and applicable law.


Identify the proposed receiving entity precisely. A trading name or corporate group label may not establish which legal entity is assuming the rights and duties.


### Obtain the required written approvals


If consent is required, request it before the transfer or new use occurs. Describe the transaction and proposed use accurately enough for the rights holder to evaluate them.


For a license to use copyrighted music, the transfer documentation should identify the original agreement, track, parties, effective date and rights being transferred. It should also address the remaining term, financial obligations and continuing restrictions.


A transfer of copyright ownership generally requires a signed writing under[Section 204(a)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/17/204) . That statutory requirement is separate from any additional consent required under the original agreement. A nonexclusive license raises a different legal analysis, but documenting permission in writing remains prudent.


A rights holder might approve an assignment, amend the existing license or issue a replacement license. The correct approach depends on whether the parties are merely changing the licensee or also changing the permitted use.


### Settle the handover details


Confirm where future notices, invoices and usage reports should go. Address outstanding payments and any practical steps needed for platform claim handling, if relevant to the arrangement.


The incoming party should receive the actual permissions, not just a seller’s summary. Preserve consent correspondence alongside the executed documents so the authorization can be demonstrated later.


Finally, carry forward the original expiration date unless the parties expressly change it. A structured process for[tracking expiring music licenses](https://usethirdchair.com/blog/how-to-track-expiring-music-licenses-across-a-catalog) helps prevent an authorized transfer from being followed by an unauthorized renewal or continued campaign.


## Who pays, and who remains liable?


There is no universal transfer fee. An agreement might permit a qualifying assignment without an additional charge, require an administrative payment or leave approval subject to negotiation. Broader uses may require a separate licensing fee regardless of whether the transfer itself costs anything.


Distinguish three financial issues: charges for transferring the agreement, charges for expanding the grant and amounts already owed under the existing deal.


Responsibility also needs explicit treatment. Assigning contractual rights does not necessarily release the original party from its duties. The incoming party may assume obligations while the outgoing party remains exposed unless the relevant parties agree otherwise.


Where a complete substitution and release are intended, counsel may use a novation or other express release arrangement. Do not infer that result from a consent letter that only approves assignment.


A transferred license to use copyrighted music also does not automatically cure earlier out-of-scope use. If the buyer or seller has already used the track without adequate permission, address that period expressly rather than assuming a later approval operates retroactively.


## Frequently asked questions


**Can I transfer a royalty-free music license to a client?** Sometimes, but “royalty-free” describes a payment model, not transfer rights. Check whether the terms cover client projects, identify the client as an authorized user or permit assignment. Delivering a completed video may be allowed even when transferring the standalone track or license is prohibited.


**Does buying a video give me its music rights?** Not automatically. Ownership of the video file or production assets is different from permission to exploit incorporated music. Obtain the relevant agreements and confirm that your entity and intended uses are covered.


**Can I sublicense the music instead of transferring the agreement?** Only if you have authority to do so. A license to use copyrighted music does not inherently include sublicensing rights. Calling an arrangement a sublicense cannot bypass restrictions on sharing permission with another business.


**Does crediting the artist make a transfer valid?** No. Attribution does not replace permission or override assignment restrictions. It may be a separate contractual requirement, but satisfying it does not establish transferability.


**Can the rights holder refuse consent?** That depends on the agreement and applicable law. Some contracts leave consent to the rights holder’s discretion, while others restrict unreasonable withholding or permit specified transfers without further approval. Check the actual standard before committing to a closing date.


## Before the next handoff


Confirm three things before transferring a licensed production: the receiving entity is authorized, every necessary music right is covered and the proposed use remains within scope. Document consent, continuing obligations and any release of the outgoing party before the handoff. If an existing agreement cannot support the transaction, obtain a replacement license before the new party publishes or distributes the content.
